title: How a Zero Trust Branch appliance is deployed: activation, ZTP, virtual machines, mainland China, upgrades and admin roles
aliases: deploying a zero trust branch appliance

prose.text: {{one-template-per-site}} The appliance models and their ports are in [[zero-trust-branch.deployment.appliances]], templates and sites in [[zero-trust-branch.deployment.templates-and-sites]], VLANs in [[zero-trust-branch.deployment.vlan]], high availability and bonding in [[zero-trust-branch.deployment.high-availability]], objects in [[zero-trust-branch.deployment.objects]] and forwarding and firewall policies in [[zero-trust-branch.deployment.policies]]. The product summary is in [[zero-trust-branch.overview]] and automation is in [[zero-trust-branch.api]].

prose.label: Before activation.
prose.text: {{tenant-provisioning}} {{upstream-ports-requirement}} The ports a hardware appliance needs are not in the captured deployment pages {{gap:hardware-activation-ports}}. {{fixed-interfaces}}

prose.label: Virtual machine ports.
prose.text: {{vm-port-activation-mgmt}} The management-plane host is named differently on another page {{divergence:management-hub-host}}. {{vm-port-upgrade-debug-wanmon}} {{vm-port-conditional}} {{vm-port-optional-dns-ntp}}

checks.do: Whether the appliance runs 8.1.2 or later, has a DHCP ISP link and is listed in the Appliance Inventory, and that it is not a VM, before choosing ZTP.
Which upgrade method the appliance's version supports according to the Appliance Version Manager page: legacy and Root FS-based on 8.0.7 or later, Root FS-based only from 8.1.1.
Whether the VLAN to be protected is enabled in the Zscaler Admin Console, since the deployment is not complete until it is.

post-activation-defaults.statement: After activation, the appliance automatically establishes an IPSec tunnel to Internet & SaaS (ZIA) through its configured WAN port; the default Zscaler routing policy allows traffic to be sent to Internet & SaaS, and the default (system) firewall policy allows traffic over LANs and WANs.

quotes: The Zero Trust Branch appliance automatically establishes an IPSec tunnel to Internet & SaaS (ZIA) through its configured WAN port
The default Zscaler routing policy allows traffic to be sent to Internet & SaaS.
The default (system) firewall policy allows traffic over LANs and WANs.

tenant-provisioning.statement: Zscaler provisions the tenant; after that it sends the super admin an email invitation that must be accepted before the super admin can access Zero Trust Branch in the Zscaler Admin Console.

quotes: After the tenant is provisioned, Zscaler sends the super admin an email invitation that must be accepted.
The super admin can then access Zero Trust Branch in the Zscaler Admin Console.
Verify that Zscaler provisioned your tenant.

one-template-per-site.statement: Each site uses a single template, which defines the Zero Trust Branch model deployed at the site and settings such as DNS server address, DHCP service type, deployment type, platform and NAT enablement.

quotes: Each site uses a single template, which defines the Zero Trust Branch model to be deployed at the site and configuration settings such as the DNS server address, DHCP service type, deployment type, platform, and NAT enablement.

fixed-interfaces.statement: Interfaces with an asterisk are fixed and cannot be changed, even on cloned templates; GE4 is fixed in an HA deployment but can be used for LAN in a standalone deployment, and the other asterisked interfaces are fixed in standalone deployments as well.

quotes: The interfaces with an asterisk (*) are fixed and cannot be changed, even on cloned templates.
The GE4 interface is fixed in an HA deployment, but in a standalone deployment it can be used for LAN. All other interfaces with an asterisk are fixed in a standalone deployment as well.

upstream-ports-requirement.statement: The appliance requires ports to be open on an upstream L3 device (a firewall or router) for initial activation and ongoing management.

quotes: A Zero Trust Branch appliance requires ports to be open on a Layer 3 (L3) device, such as an upstream firewall or a router, for initial activation and ongoing management.

vm-port-activation-mgmt.statement: The VM deployment page lists TCP 443 outbound to gwactivation.goairgap.com for appliance activation and TCP 1883 outbound to hub3.goairgap.com for management-plane communication, each marked a mandatory requirement.

quotes: | TCP 443 | Outbound | gwactivation.goairgap.com | This port is used for appliance activation. This is a mandatory requirement. |
| TCP 1883 | Outbound | hub3.goairgap.com | This port is required for management-plane communication. This is a mandatory requirement. |

vm-port-upgrade-debug-wanmon.statement: The VM deployment page lists, as mandatory, TCP 443 outbound to dl.cloudsmith.io for software upgrades, TCP 443 outbound to gateway.<cloud>.net for WAN monitoring, and UDP 51820 outbound to wg.goairgap.com for remote debugging.

quotes: | TCP 443 | Outbound | dl.cloudsmith.io | This port is required for software upgrades. This is a mandatory requirement. |
| TCP 443 | Outbound | gateway.<cloud>.net | This port is required for WAN monitoring. This is a mandatory requirement. |
| UDP 51820 | Outbound | wg.goairgap.com | This port is required for remote debugging. This is a mandatory requirement. |

vm-port-conditional.statement: The VM deployment page lists conditional ports: UDP 443 with access type Inbound and the public-routable IP address of the spoke appliance as host, for Routed Tunnels in a Hub-and-Spoke model; UDP 500, UDP 4500 and ESP (IP protocol 50) outbound if connecting to Internet & SaaS; TCP 443 outbound to config.zscaler.com/private.zscaler.com/zpa, prod.zpath.net and private.zscaler.com if connecting to Private Access (ZPA).

quotes: | UDP 443 | Inbound | Public-routable IP address of the spoke appliance used for tunnel establishment | This port is required for Routed Tunnels if Zero Trust Branch appliances are deployed in the Hub-and-Spoke model. |
| UDP 500 UDP 4500 ESP - IP Protocol 50 | Outbound |
This port is required if the Zero Trust Branch appliance must connect to Internet & SaaS.
| TCP 443 | Outbound | config.zscaler.com/private.zscaler.com/zpa prod.zpath.net private.zscaler.com | This port is required if the Zero Trust Branch appliance must connect to Private Access (ZPA). |

vm-port-optional-dns-ntp.statement: The VM deployment page lists UDP 53 outbound to the DNS service IP if specific DNS servers are used, and UDP 123 outbound to 0.pool.ntp.org through 3.pool.ntp.org if specific NTP servers are used.

quotes: | UDP 53 | Outbound | IP address of DNS service | This port is required if the Zero Trust Branch appliances must use specific DNS servers for name resolution. |
| UDP 123 | Outbound | 0.pool.ntp.org 1.pool.ntp.org 2.pool.ntp.org 3.pool.ntp.org | This port is required if the Zero Trust Branch appliance must use specific NTP servers for time synchronization. |

console-serial-params.statement: The serial console connection uses 115,200 baud, 8 data bits, 1 stop bit, no parity and XON/XOFF flow control.

quotes: Baud Rate: 115,200
Data Bits: 8
Stop Bits: 1
Parity: None
Flow Control: XON/XOFF

activation-subinterface.statement: Zscaler supports one subinterface per WAN interface, but activation is supported over the WAN main interface (which the page calls tagged), not over a subinterface (which the page calls untagged).

quotes: Zscaler supports one subinterface per WAN interface. However, Zero Trust Branch activation is supported over the WAN interface on the main interface (which is tagged), not on a subinterface (which is untagged).

activation-code-method.statement: The activation-code method uses the activation code saved when the site was added and requires configuring the appliance with the same parameters used when the site was created; the web proxy step is required only if the appliance is deployed behind a firewall.

quotes: Before you activate the appliance, you must configure it with the same parameters you configured when you created the site in the Zscaler Admin Console.
b. Configure the web proxy (Required only if the Zero Trust Branch appliance is deployed behind a firewall)
This method uses the activation code that you saved during the Adding a Site procedure in the Zscaler Admin Console.

activation-url-method.statement: The activation-URL method carries the WAN interface configuration and the activation code in the URL saved when the site was created; a laptop connected directly to the management port gets an IP address from the appliance.

quotes: The URL contains the configuration data for the WAN interface and the activation code.
Connect a laptop directly to the management port on the appliance. The laptop automatically gets an IP address directly from the appliance.

site-state-values.statement: After activation, the site State is Standalone for a standalone appliance, Active for the primary node of an HA cluster and Standby for the secondary node.

quotes: Standalone for a standalone appliance
Active for the primary node of an HA cluster
Standby for the secondary node of an HA cluster

vm-post-update-state.statement: After activating a VM, the gateway runs background scripts for a few minutes during which the site State shows Post Update; when they finish, State changes to Standalone.

quotes: This process takes a few minutes and during this period, the State column for the site in the Zscaler Admin Console shows Post Update.
when the background processes are completed, the State column is updated to Standalone
After the activation, the Zero Trust Branch VM gateway runs the necessary scripts in the background.

lan-trunk-requirement.statement: To process multiple VLANs, the switchport connected to the appliance's LAN-side interface must be a trunk port that allows the VLANs to be protected.

quotes: To process multiple VLANs, the switchport connecting to the LAN-side interface of the Zero Trust Branch appliance must be configured as a trunk port, and it must allow the VLANs that need to be protected by Zero Trust Branch.

vlan-enable-required.statement: The deployment is not complete until the VLAN to be protected is enabled in the Zscaler Admin Console; for an existing production VLAN the default gateway IP must match the existing SVI address, and for an untagged port the VLAN ID is 1.

quotes: Zero Trust Branch deployment is not complete until the VLAN to be protected is enabled in the Zscaler Admin Console.
make sure that the default gateway IP address is the same as the existing Switch Virtual Interface (SVI) address for that VLAN.
If you are configuring an untagged port, enter 1 in the VLAN ID field.

verify-deployment.statement: To verify the deployment, check that client traffic goes to the internet via Internet & SaaS (ip.zscaler.com) and that the Auto-provisioned Tunnels tab shows Status Up; editing the IPSec tunnel configuration is optional and only if directed by Zscaler Support.

quotes: Go to ip.zscaler.com.
On the Auto-provisioned Tunnels tab, verify the value in the Status column is Up.
(Optional) Only if directed by Zscaler Support, edit the IPSec tunnel configuration for the site:

ztp-support.statement: ZTP is supported on appliances running version 8.1.2 or later and is not supported for VM deployment.

quotes: ZTP is supported on Zero Trust Branch appliances running version 8.1.2 or later, and is not supported for VM deployment.

ztp-prerequisites.statement: ZTP requires an appliance on 8.1.2 or later, an ISP link that supports DHCP, and the appliance serial number listed in the Appliance Inventory; ZTP does not work with static IP addresses.

quotes: The appliance is running 8.1.2 or later.
The ISP link used for ZTP supports DHCP.
The appliance serial number is listed in the Appliance Inventory.
ZTP does not work with static IP addresses.

ztp-ports-8-1-2.statement: For version 8.1.2, the ZTP-enabled WAN port is ge3 on ZT400, ge5 on ZT600, ge2 on ZT800 and ge2 on ZT8010; by default the gateway listens for ZTP only on the ZTP-enabled WAN ports, so the WAN cable must be connected to such a port before power-on.

quotes: For ZTP, the gateway listens for ZTP only on the ZTP-enabled WAN port(s) by default. To onboard via ZTP, connect the WAN cable to the ZTP-enabled port before powering on the appliance.

### WAN Ports by Model for 8.1.2
- ZT400: ge3
- ZT600: ge5
- ZT800: ge2
- ZT8010: ge2

ztp-ports-8-1-2p1.statement: For 8.1.2P1 and later, the ZTP-enabled WAN ports are ge3 (ZT400), ge5 and ge6 (ZT600), ge2 and ge7 (ZT800), and ge2 and xe7 (ZT8010).

quotes:
### WAN Ports by Model for 8.1.2P1 and Later
- ZT400: ge3
- ZT600: ge5, ge6
- ZT800: ge2, ge7
- ZT8010: ge2, xe7

ztp-default-templates.statement: The ZTP page lists default templates: ZT400 zt400-ha-default, zt400-standalone-default and zt400-standalone-dualwan-default; ZT600 zt600-ha-default, zt600-enhanced-ha-default and zt600-standalone-default; ZT800 and ZT8010 follow the same ha, enhanced-ha and standalone pattern.

quotes: | ZT400 | zt400-ha-default | zt400-standalone-default zt400-standalone-dualwan-default |
| ZT600 | zt600-ha-default zt600-enhanced-ha-default | zt600-standalone-default |
| ZT800 | zt800-ha-default zt800-enhanced-ha-default | zt800-standalone-default |
| ZT8010 | zt8010-ha-default zt8010-enhanced-ha-default | zt8010-standalone-default |

ztp-verify.statement: The show ztp activation-state command confirms Authentication State true, ZTP Device true, the current ZTP server, serial number and TPM serial number for a correctly configured appliance, and show ztp tpm-attest validates the hardware identity against the TPM endorsement key certificate.

quotes: To confirm the authentication state, ZTP device, ZTP server, appliance serial number, and TPM serial number, use the command show ztp activation-state.
Authentication State: true
ZTP Device: true
To validate the hardware identity against the TPM endorsement key certificate, use the command show ztp tpm-attest.

appliance-inventory.statement: Appliance Inventory serial numbers are auto-populated during ordering; missing serial numbers are requested through Zscaler Support.

quotes: Serial numbers are auto-populated during the ordering process. If certain serial numbers are not available in the inventory, request additional serial numbers by contacting Zscaler Support.

china-support.statement: Mainland China proxy use is supported for appliances on Zero Trust Branch 8.1.2-P1 and later; a support ticket with the appliance serial number requests support, and the appliance cannot connect to the proxy until it is authorized to do so.

quotes: Zscaler supports mainland China proxy use for appliances with Zero Trust Branch version 8.1.2-P1 and later.
Although you can do this after configuration, your appliance cannot connect to the proxy until it is authorized to do so.
Open a support ticket with Zscaler Support to provide the serial number and request that your appliance be supported for use in mainland China.

china-cnp.statement: For mainland China, a dedicated connection proxy provides a premium connection to the cloud control plane; it is enabled in zscaler-console via option 1 Configure Appliance, option 3 Configure CNP Client.

quotes: This dedicated proxy provides a premium connection to its cloud control plane, mitigating connection challenges associated with restricted network environments.
Select option 3 - Configure CNP Client.
Log in with an admin account, via either a console cable or SSH, and enter zscaler-console.
Select option 1 - Configure Appliance.

vm-sizing.statement: The VM page gives two sizing options: 4 vCPU, 16 GB memory, 4 vNICs, 500K sessions and 500 endpoints, with 10 Gbps throughput for unencrypted LAN-to-LAN or LAN-to-WAN flows; or 8 vCPU, 32 GB, 8 vNICs, 1 million sessions and 1,000 endpoints, with 20 Gbps for the same flows; each with 256 GB storage.

quotes: | CPU | 4 vCPU | 8 vCPU |
| Memory | 16 GB | 32 GB |
| Storage | 256 GB | 256 GB |
| Ports | 4 x vNICs (VMXNET3 recommended) | 8 x vNICs (VMXNET3 recommended) |
| Throughput (Unencrypted LAN-to-LAN or LAN-to-WAN flows) | 10 Gbps | 20 Gbps |
| Sessions | 500K | 1 Million |
| Number of Endpoints | 500 | 1,000 |

vm-port-mapping.statement: In the VM port mapping, ge3 is Management, ge2, ge7 and ge8 are WAN, and ge1, ge4, ge5 and ge6 are LAN.

quotes: | 1 | ge1 | LAN |
| 2 | ge2 | WAN |
| 3 | ge3 | Management |
| 7 | ge7 | WAN |
| 8 | ge8 | WAN |
| 4 | ge4 | LAN |
| 5 | ge5 | LAN |
| 6 | ge6 | LAN |

vm-esxi-portgroups.statement: On ESXi, the LAN port group uses VLAN ID 4095 as a trunk group, with Promiscuous mode, MAC address changes and Forged transmits set to Accept; the WAN port group is an access group with a VLAN ID between 0 and 4094.

quotes: Enter 4095 as the LAN port group must be a trunk port group.
Click Security and select Accept for the following options:
Enter a VLAN ID (value between 0 and 4094) as the WAN port group must be an access port group.
Promiscuous mode
MAC address changes
Forged transmits

vm-esxi-settings.statement: The ESXi VM wizard selects ESXi 6.7 compatibility, Linux guest OS family with Ubuntu Linux (64-bit), and EFI firmware.

quotes: Compatibility: Select ESXi 6.7 virtual machine from the drop-down menu.
Guest OS version: Select Ubuntu Linux (64-bit) from the drop-down menu.
go to Boot Options and select EFI from the drop-down menu as the firmware.
Guest OS family: Select Linux from the drop-down menu.

vm-iso-source.statement: The VM page says the ISO image is obtained from the Zscaler Admin Console in its prerequisites and from Zscaler Support in the wizard step.

quotes: The Zero Trust Branch ISO image is obtained from the Zscaler Admin Console.
upload the Zero Trust Branch ISO file obtained from Zscaler Support.

avm-intro.statement: The Appliance Version Manager page says release 8.0.7 introduced Appliance Version Manager, a full image-based upgrade system that supports downgrades, and that before 8.0.7 the legacy incremental method upgraded only selected packages and did not support downgrades.

quotes: Zero Trust Branch release 8.0.7 introduces a new upgrade mechanism called Appliance Version Manager
the software upgrade process is transitioned to a full image–based system, including support for downgrades.
Prior to release 8.0.7, Zero Trust Branch used the legacy incremental upgrade method where only selected packages were upgraded and downgrades were not supported.

avm-methods.statement: The Appliance Version Manager page says appliances on version 8.0.7 or later support both the legacy and Root FS-based Appliance Version Manager methods, and that from version 8.1.1 only the Root FS-based Appliance Version Manager is supported.

quotes: Zero Trust Branch supports both legacy and Root FS-based Appliance Version Manager methods for upgrading appliances running version 8.0.7 or later.
Starting with version 8.1.1, you can upgrade using only the Root FS-based Appliance Version Manager, as the legacy method is no longer supported.

avm-two-stages.statement: An image upgrade has two stages: downloading and installing the image, which needs no downtime, and activating it, which needs a reboot during scheduled downtime.

quotes: This step does not require downtime and can be performed at any time.
This step requires a system reboot, which must be performed during a scheduled downtime.
Image upgrade using Appliance Version Manager includes the following two stages:
1. Download and install the image.
2. Activate the image.

avm-three-images.statement: The Appliance Version Manager page says it stores up to three image versions (8.0.7 or later); one downloaded image is always the default (factory default) image, which cannot be deleted and is what the appliance rolls back to on a factory reset.

quotes: allows you to download and store up to three Zero Trust Branch image versions (8.0.7 or later).
One downloaded image (also known as the factory default image) is always marked as default
If any unknown issue occurs and requires a factory reset, the appliance rolls back to this image.
The default image cannot be deleted.

avm-factory-reset.statement: A factory reset (UI Delete Site, UI RMA, or airgap-console factory-reset) erases the data partition and restores the factory default Root FS.

quotes: Performing a factory reset (UI Delete Site, UI RMA, or airgap-console factory-reset) erases the data partition and restores the factory default Root FS.

avm-downgrade.statement: Image downgrade is supported up to version 8.0.7; for an Active/Standby pair, downgrade the Standby appliance first, switch over and validate, then downgrade the Active one.

quotes: Image downgrade is supported up to version 8.0.7.
you must first downgrade the appliance in Standby state, switch over, validate the action, and then downgrade the second appliance in Active state.

rbac-predefined-roles.statement: Zero Trust Branch has no custom roles; the predefined roles are Super Admin, Network Admin, Security Admin and Viewer.

quotes: Zero Trust Branch does not have custom roles. The following predefined roles are available:
- Super Admin: The super admin has the highest level of privileges.
- Network Admin: The network admin is responsible for configuring and maintaining all network-related components.
- Security Admin: The security admin is tasked with managing and enforcing the platform's overall security posture.
- Viewer: The viewer role grants users read-only access, including access to associated logs.

rbac-role-scope.statement: The network admin role operates independently of the platform's security policy configurations; the security admin can initiate device quarantine and trigger the Ransomware Kill Switch; the viewer cannot alter any configuration settings.

quotes: while operating independently of the platform's security policy configurations.
the security admin is authorized to initiate device quarantine actions in response to anomalous or malicious activity.
This role is also responsible for triggering the Ransomware Kill Switch
Viewers cannot alter any configuration settings
The network admin is responsible for configuring and maintaining all network-related components.

rbac-super-admin.statement: The super admin has full access to security policy configuration, network settings, site and template management and user account creation, and can audit system logs, apply firmware updates, initiate failover and restore the system.

quotes: This role has full access to security policy configuration, network settings (including routing and VLANs), site and template management, as well as user account creation and administration.
Super admins are authorized to audit system logs, apply firmware updates, initiate failover operations, and restore the system as required.

rbac-identity.statement: Beginning with version 8.0.1, Zero Trust Branch uses Authentication Service as its sole identity and authentication management service; users and groups are managed in the Zscaler Admin Console under the Zero Trust Branch service.

quotes: Beginning with version 8.0.1, Zero Trust Branch is enabled with Authentication Service as its sole identity and authentication management service.
To add and manage Zero Trust Branch users and user groups, log in to the Zscaler Admin Console and select the Zero Trust Branch service.

management-hub-host.summary: The VM deployment page names hub3.goairgap.com for TCP 1883 management-plane traffic, while the activation-issues page names hub.goairgap.com for the same port.

positions.says: TCP 1883 outbound goes to hub3.goairgap.com for management-plane communication.

quotes: | TCP 1883 | Outbound | hub3.goairgap.com | This port is required for management-plane communication. This is a mandatory requirement. |

positions.says: The appliance must be allowed outbound connections to hub.goairgap.com on TCP 1883.

quotes: hub.goairgap.com (TCP: 1883)

management-hub-host.impact: An upstream firewall rule written from one page may omit the host the other page names.

hardware-activation-ports.title: Which upstream ports a hardware appliance needs open for activation and upgrade
hardware-activation-ports.detail: The VM deployment page's port table lists TCP 443, TCP 1883 and UDP 51820 outbound among others. The hardware appliance port list is on a separate page about the ports that need to be open for appliance activation and upgrade, which these deployment pages do not reproduce; the activation-issues page names only the TCP 1883 and UDP 51820 outbound ports.
